title: setupDataSources seeds both legacy DatasourceSrv and the async @grafana/runtime cache
answers: getDataSourceInstanceList returns empty in alerting tests
useDataSourceInstance hooks return no data sources in tests
Why does my mocked data source not show up via the new runtime APIs?
How to register mock data sources for alerting frontend tests
body:
Symptom: alerting frontend tests that call setupDataSources get correct results from DatasourceSrv-based code, but getDataSourceInstanceList / useDataSourceInstance* hooks return empty.
Root cause: those newer @grafana/runtime APIs read from a separate async data source cache, not from the legacy DatasourceSrv that setupDataSources used to seed alone (public/app/features/alerting/unified/testSetup/datasources.ts:setupDataSources).
Fix pattern: setupDataSources now also calls setDataSourceInstanceSettings from '@grafana/runtime/internal' with the same datasourceSettings map and default name, keeping both caches in sync.
Constraints: any test helper or code path that registers mock/real data sources must seed both DatasourceSrv (via setDataSourceSrv) and the async cache (via setDataSourceInstanceSettings) — seeding only one leaves the other API surface empty. Do not hand-build a separate map to call setDataSourceInstanceSettings a second time; reuse setupDataSources instead.
applies: Alerting (and any) frontend tests that mock data sources via public/app/features/alerting/unified/testSetup/datasources.ts

search: The setupDataSources helper in public/app/features/alerting/unified/testSetup/datasources.ts seeds both the legacy DatasourceSrv and the separate @grafana/runtime async data source cache by calling setDataSourceInstanceSettings from '@grafana/runtime/internal' with the same datasourceSettings map and default name. Constraint: tests that mock data sources must seed both caches simultaneously; seeding only one leaves the other API surface empty, causing getDataSourceInstanceList and useDataSourceInstance* hooks to return empty while legacy DatasourceSrv-based code works correctly. Do not hand-build a separate map for a second call to setDataSourceInstanceSettings; reuse setupDataSources to keep both in sync. Applies to alerting and any frontend tests that register mock or real data sources.
